subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized lava golem module in Genshin Impact's aesthetic—basalt plates, molten glowing seams, Pyro-like glyph textures, cel-shaded colors—aiming for a well-structured TypeScript build with roughly 180-340 parts since I can't test the API directly.

Now I'm sketching the import list from the agentic-3js-builder library plus glow and toon shading kits, then designing the golem's skeleton starting with a hip root and a spine chain built from catmull-rom points, working out how many joints each knot span produces so the naming matches correctly.

Next I'm placing the head sunk between massive shoulders, adding a separate jaw joint, then moving to the arm rig with shoulders set wide apart and huge hanging fists in a slightly outward resting pose.

Elbow should bend back and slightly outward for the A-pose. I'm thinking I could make the limbs hexagonal basalt column sweeps—faceted, chunky, and thematically fitting—with plates attached on top, using varying radius along the chain.

For the style, I'm going with a Genshin-like cel-shaded look: dark basalt tones paired with glowing orange-to-yellow lava gradients, using two-tone cel paints and emissive glow for the molten seams between plates. I want a glowing core visible through a chest window, plus glowing textured eyes, so I'm starting to sketch out the SVG textures needed for those elements.

Still writing SVG textures...

I also need a glowing ground rune circle and a lava-glow jaw interior, plus a basalt mottled paint for the rock surfaces.

Since painted surfaces can't emit glow, lava parts should stay flat-colored. For the cracked basalt plates, I'm thinking of using a cell-based paint that detects the seams between cell regions and colors those thin lines as molten lava, giving a cracked, glowing-vein look across the rock.

Defining patch and sweep paints...

Now I'm working out the overall geometry layout: total golem height around 3.4m standing on a faceted base platform. I'll set the base thickness to 0.16 so the top surface acts as the floor reference, with feet positioned to sink slightly into it, then start placing the legs from that floor height.

For the legs I'm sizing short, stout hex columns with hip sockets around y=1.45 and feet targeting the floor, checking the reach distance against two-segment lengths (thigh and shin) to figure out how much knee bend is needed, settling on roughly 0.78 and 0.72 for those segments.

For the leg chain I'm using three points—hip, knee, foot—with the third named joint landing as the tip at the foot target, then deciding to skip separate toe joints for simplicity and just place a foot block around the ankle, while considering whether to add simple finger joints to the fists to satisfy the digit-separation requirement.

For hands, I'm sketching three stubby fingers per fist as short chains (two or three points each, giving one or two spans), swept with hex columns, pointing forward and downward in a relaxed splayed pose coming out of a blunt stone fist.

Now I'm tallying joint budget: hips, three spine segments, head, jaw fused with head, shoulders, two arms each with shoulder-elbow-wrist chains, sixteen finger joints across both hands, two legs with three joints each, rigid pauldrons sitting on the shoulder bone, and a small animated flame chain on the back for a fan-like motion, plus some dorsal vent joints -- all staying comfortably under the 160 joint ceiling.

I'm skipping a tail and deciding floating orbital rocks don't need joints, just attaching to the chest bone directly. I'm weighing whether to add hinged chest door plates flanking the core for a nice opening effect, but deciding it adds too much complexity and dropping it in favor of simplicity, then starting to lay out the torso loft stations beginning with the hips.

Writing torso loft stations...

Actually, let me go with `{ngon: 6}` for the torso instead — a hexagonal cross-section with a vertex pointing along the normal direction gives flat faces at the left/right sides, which reads nicely as a blocky puppet torso.

I'll shift to a box-section torso instead to get clean flat chest/back panels for armor plating, then plan loft calls using a points array with position/width/height per level. For the armor, I'll add separately-placed box plates as overlays — chest plates with bevels, dorsal basalt spikes along the back — rather than trying to bake everything into the loft profile.

For positioning things on the torso, I'll use a surface-hit helper that queries the loft surface by azimuth/elevation around a center point and returns null if nothing's hit, wrapping calls in guards. The chest core will be a glowing octagonal frame with a recessed emissive panel, placed just in front of the torso's front surface using the hit helper to find the correct offset.

I'm attaching the glow decal to the chest hit point, then building a ring of eight basalt spikes around it facing outward from the core center to form a housing.

Next I'm sketching the head: a small block offset forward from the torso top, with a brow ridge and eye decals to add.

Now I'm planning the jaw joint hinging at the back-bottom of the head, with glowing lava teeth and an orange-lit mouth interior between the jaws, plus basalt horns sweeping up from the head like a flame crest.

For shoulders, I'm designing bulky pauldrons from low-poly rock shapes (icosahedron or dodecahedron geometry) with glowing lava spheres peeking through the gaps between rock chunks for a molten effect.

I'm thinking through the color palette now -- deep purple-black basalt, vivid orange lava, and gold-toned "#d9b36a" trim for ancient rune bands on the forearms, keeping everything clean and cel-shaded in a Genshin-style look. For the flame elements, I'm planning glowing flame-textured cards arranged on the back and around the head crown, mounted on scattered hit points across the shoulders and back surface.

Scattering flame cards across the torso back...

Edge-on is bad, so I realize cards need to lean toward the flow direction so they're visible from behind rather than disappearing edge-on; leaning about 70° toward upward flow makes cards stand up like flames, with their width running perpendicular to both the axis and flow directions.

Actually, simpler approach: use upward-pointing frames with default lean so cards stand straight up, letting the flow default flatten onto the horizontal plane so the card normal faces front/back and width runs sideways -- making them visible from both directions, and I'll mark them cross-sided for full visibility. I'll place flame wisps manually at shoulder and back positions, letting literal frames snap to the nearest joint by bone proximity, and add small floating glowing embers the same way.

Floating lava rocks around the base get attached to the hips bone since they're static. I'm sketching out the texture list needed: a glowing eye, chest core emblem, flame card, gold rune band for decals, a glowing ground magic circle, molten crack decals for armor plates, small ember spark stars, and maybe a mouth texture, along with basalt and lava paint materials.

Writing import statements...

Defining the lava color palette and basalt cel-shaded materials, then building molten and patchwork paint textures for the plate armor seams.

Defining plate paint variants...

With ~60m² total area that gives roughly 9mm texels, which feels acceptable even with blocky cel-shaded edges. I'll stick with 1024 for safety rather than bumping to 2048 and a heavier 4096 atlas, and I'm reconsidering whether flat colors lit naturally by the scene might be simpler than full cel shading for the small parts.

I'm deciding to use paints for the big pieces and flat colors for the small ones, keeping the color limit around 20 out of a possible 64. Now I'm sketching out the golem's build function, starting with the root setup, random seed, and floor height constant, then planning the base rock platform as a nine-sided cylinder anchored to the hips bone, making sure the hip joint exists before referencing it, followed by a glowing lava pool ring beneath the feet.

Writing lava texture plane...

Setting up the hip joint and spine chain with a catmull-rom curve through four points, parenting it correctly and naming the spine segments.

I'm working out the neck and head joints, trying to figure out how many points and names map to each short chain segment, and whether the head attaches at the end of the neck.

Checking total height with horns around 3.7-3.9 feels right for a large lava golem, so I'll keep the scale as is. Now I'm working out the torso loft stations, defining chest width and height at increasing y positions so the neck exits cleanly at the top near 2.85.

Writing loft stations...

Then I think about pauldrons covering the shoulder joints outside the torso edge, and plan the pelvis/skirt as faceted hanging plates like armor tassets around the waist.

Adjusting the plate orientation so thickness points outward and the vertical dimension aligns upward, I'm positioning each plate center at the ring point around the hips, accounting for the elliptical loft radius at that height.

Since the plates were slightly floating relative to the actual surface, I'm considering switching to a loop-based approach that follows the torso's true surface normals instead of a fixed radius, using a point and direction to define the belt plane and checking it falls within the torso's loft bounds.

For orienting each plate correctly, I need the actual surface normal at each position rather than just the path tangent, so I'm planning to query the nearest surface hit at each loop point and use its normal to orient the stick geometry outward.

For side wall hits, z corresponds to world up with x running forward/back; for front-facing hits, x runs toward the model's right and z runs upward along the surface, so these conventions line up consistently. This means I can position the skirt tassets along the loop at y=1.55 with plates hanging down, spanning roughly 1.27 to 1.82, which nicely tucks below where the pelvis loft bottoms out at 1.45.

Now I'm setting the plate vertical size to 0.5 centered at y=1.5 so it covers the lower torso and hangs below, with the loop positioned at y=1.55 to get the plate center where I want it. For the belt, I'm sweeping a lava belt loop at y=1.78 with a thin glowing profile. Moving on to torso decorations, I'm thinking through the core housing decal, chest rib seams, and back detailing.

Now I'm scattering dorsal rock bumps and lava vent flames across the back, plus trapezius rocks bridging shoulder to neck. For the arms, I'm computing the limb geometry between shoulder and hand points using distance and bend hints to get a mild elbow bend, then sweeping the upper arm and forearm with slightly different radii for a bulkier fist side.

I'm using a faceted hexagonal cross-section for the arm sweep, tapering the radius along the chain from shoulder to wrist for a natural limb shape, then attaching a boxy fist geometry at the wrist joint offset to hang below the forearm.

I'll compute the hand direction vector from the arm points, then size the fist box roughly .55 wide and deep with its length aligned along that direction, keeping the default roll so the box's side stays close to the model's right.

Now I'm working out how the fingers attach: with no explicit up vector, the aim direction maps to the box's forward axis, so for a downward-pointing arm the box's local axes rotate accordingly. I'm placing the fist center partway along the hand direction and defining the bottom edge of the fist as the anchor point where four two-joint finger chains will start, spaced out from that base.

Writing finger positions...

Still shaping finger geometry...

I need unique naming per finger segment and side, and I'm confirming chain() accepts point arrays directly for building polyline paths with knots at each vertex. For pauldrons, I'm deciding they should attach to the shoulder bone so they move naturally with arm rotation rather than staying fixed on the chest.

Now I'm working out the pauldron geometry: a dodecahedron shoulder piece with flat-shaded rock coloring, plus stacked spiked layers above it using basalt cones, and a glowing lava torus ring positioned at the seam beneath the pauldron, oriented along the arm's rotation axis.

Next I'm adding an elbow spike using the spike-building function, anchored to the elbow joint with a hexagonal cross-section, then placing a decal for runes along the forearm band.

I'll position the decal near the surface using the arm's point plus an outward offset, then think about sizing—since the forearm is tall and narrow, the rune band should probably run vertically along the limb rather than wide and horizontal.

Now I'm sketching stacked glyph boxes for the runes texture and figuring out whether mirroring is needed for the opposite side, deciding it's not worth worrying about for a glyph-style decal. Then I shift to leg geometry, setting the hip socket and foot target positions and working out the distance between them for the leg segment lengths.

Trying different hip/ankle heights and leg segment lengths to get a believable squat stance, landing on roughly 0.65-length segments with the knee bowing outward about 0.44 units -- a stout, thick-legged golem posture.

I'm setting up the leg bone chain (hip, knee, ankle) parented to the hips, sizing the leg's tapered radius profile, adding a dodecahedron knee guard offset slightly forward, and starting the foot block geometry.

For the foot, I'm positioning it so it sits just on the floor with its box dimensions extending slightly forward, and considering whether to add separate toe joints as digit bones attached to the ankle for additional rig detail.

I'll give each foot three toe chains, spaced side to side, built as single-span hexagonal prisms with pointed end caps acting like claws, positioned so their bottoms just meet the floor.

For the leg itself, I'm checking the ankle and foot box placement against the floor line to make sure the leg sweep's rounded cap overlaps cleanly with the foot box without gapping, then connecting the hip joint as the parent for the leg bone chain.

Now moving to head details: I'm placing the skull box, brow ridge, and face plate relative to the head bone's local frame, and setting up the eye decals as glowing textured planes positioned against the skull's front face.

For angry slanted eyes, I need mirrored geometry between left and right — flipping the scale would cause winding/culling problems, so I'm considering using separate mirrored eye textures instead.

Actually, a simpler fix: I can just flip the UV coordinates on one geometry (u = 1-u) to mirror the same texture without duplicating assets. Now I'm moving on to the jaw — placing an upper jaw block under the skull front, working out where the skull's vertical extent sits so the jaw aligns correctly.

Positioning the jaw joint, upper and lower jaw boxes, and a glowing lava gap between them so the mouth reads as open when needed, plus small cone teeth along the upper jaw.

Now for horns, I'm sketching bezier paths off the head using local coordinate offsets for right/up/forward, but I need to double check the sidedness convention since "right" maps to world −X and I want the horn on the +X side, so I should use a "left" offset instead.

For coloring, I'm planning a dark basalt base for the horn with a glowing lava-colored spike at the tip, since sweep color bands can't do a true glow effect, so a separate glowing cone mesh at the horn's tip position is the better approach.

I'm switching to simpler curved sweep horns using bezier paths with tip tangent computed from the last two points, capping each with a small glowing lava spike. For details beyond horns, I'm considering adding a few crest rocks on top of the head and flame cards on the shoulders/back rather than behind the horns.

I'm scattering dodecahedron rocks across the back (filtered by position/normal), then designing pectoral armor plates as extruded pentagon outlines positioned on either side of the chest core.

Working out mirroring: I can flip the plate to the other side by reversing the sign on the x-direction vector, since the extrusion geometry should handle orientation safely regardless of the thickness axis flipping.

For positioning the pectoral plate, I'll raycast down onto the torso surface near the chest to find the actual skin z-depth at that point, then offset the plate center slightly outward from that hit point with a thin protrusion thickness, connecting its top edge toward the shoulders.

Checking the outline coordinates, I realize the plates would collide with the core ring at the center, so I need to shift the plate x-position outward to clear the core's radius while staying within the torso's half-width at that height.

Positioning pectoral slabs so they slightly overlap the torso near the neck, which should be fine visually. I'm skipping extra waist seam lines since the belt already covers that area, and deciding to place a crack decal on the torso belly instead of the thigh or forearm for better visual impact.

Adding a mirrored crack decal on the back, then planning five orbiting dodecahedra rocks with inner lava glow at varying heights, plus around 30 randomly placed glowing ember cards and a set of flame frames along the upper back and shoulders.

I'm tallying up the total mesh count across torso, skirt, arms, legs, head, and floating rocks, landing around 170 parts, and checking whether leg plating needs more detail.

Now I'm planning gold Genshin-style accents: torus rings at the wrists and neck, and an octahedron gem on the belt buckle for the lava gem accent. Next up is writing the eye texture as an SVG.

Writing SVG code...

I'm reasoning through the eye asymmetry: the inner corner should sit lower for an angry look, so the drawn shape works for the left side as-is but needs mirroring for the right.

Now I'm designing the core symbol as a layered SVG—dark ring base, orange gradient disc, and a pyro-style emblem with rays and a central diamond.

Still writing SVG code...

Still writing flame SVG shapes...

Still writing SVG code...

Still writing icon paths...

Now I'm planning a cracked-earth SVG with jagged branching fault lines in orange and yellow, using a thick orange stroke layered under a thinner yellow stroke for a molten glow effect, plus considering a sun emblem detail.

With seven textures finalized (eye, core, flame, ember, circle, runes, crack), I'm moving to code: a helper for generating flat-shaded dodecahedron rocks for pauldrons, and setting up distinct obsidian and dark color constants to differentiate rock variants.

Still writing color palette constants...

I'm defining a helper to query surface hit points at a given azimuth/elevation using the skin's around method, keeping types inferred rather than explicit, and confirming that the torso surface accepts the Sweep from the loft directly.

Now I'm scattering points across the surface with a filter for downward-facing, upper-region normals, then sticking rocks onto those points with slight random scale variation and embedding depth for a flat, embedded look.

Next I'm thinking through using `along` to walk ten points around a waist loop and stick alternating box geometries there as a belt detail, checking that the callback signature and box orientation relative to the surface normal make sense for a front-facing hit.

I'm now second-guessing the embed math: if the stuck part's origin sinks by embed times its own height, and the box is centered on that origin, then half the box would poke through the surface rather than the whole thing protruding outward as intended—so I may need to flip the sign or rethink how embed is applied for centered geometries like a box.

I'm setting up a ray cast to find the core-fitting location on the torso, then clamping to a fallback position if the ray misses, and sketching out a decal call that places the core texture at that point with a slight outward lift to avoid z-fighting.

Now I'm designing the rim pieces as a ring of 8 wedge boxes positioned radially around the core, oriented so their depth axis points outward along the surface normal.

Still working out torus orientation...

Now I'm sizing the gorget ring to match the torso's width and depth proportions, then placing a dodecahedron near the chest for a trapezius-like detail. I'm starting the main build function with a seeded random generator for the basalt lava golem.

Next I'm defining the skeleton hierarchy—hips as the root joint, a spine chain built from a curved path through several control points, and a neck chain branching off the chest joint toward where the head will attach.

Now I'm adding the head and jaw joints, positioning the jaw relative to the head's local orientation so it can aim forward and downward. Then I'm setting up a symmetric loop to build out left and right arms, defining shoulder and hand positions for each side...

Working through limb bend directions...

The limb function returns three points, which I'll feed into a chain call to build the arm, naming the chain and its joints with a side suffix so left/right stay unique.

I'm checking that passing a Vector3 array as points works with the chain API, and confirming the joints array gives shoulder and elbow while the tip (possibly nullable) gives the wrist—so destructuring `arm.joints` plus `arm.tip!` should correctly map the three named points.

Now I'm sweeping varying radii along the arm chain with a hexagonal cross-section and rounded caps, then placing a glowing lava torus ring partway up the upper arm by computing direction vectors between joint points and offsetting from the shoulder.

Still placing the pauldron geometry...

Adding a second pauldron layer with rock texturing offset from the shoulder, plus spike details using the dark rock color for contrast.

I'm also thinking about adding small glowing lava accents peeking through gaps between the rock plates, maybe a small gem-like nugget embedded near the front of the pauldron for visual interest.

Writing elbow spike code...

Now I'm thinking through the forearm accessories: a gold torus bracer at the forearm midpoint and another near the wrist, plus a rune decal placed partway along the forearm's outer face.

I'm uncertain whether the decal point should sit exactly on the surface or slightly inset, so I'll approximate using the apothem radius for the hex face and settle on roughly 0.3 as a reasonable placement. Now moving on to positioning the fist geometry relative to the point array.

Still working out finger placement and orientation...

Sweeping finger geometry with tapered radii...

Building the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, verifying the reach distance stays within the segment lengths so the limb can actually extend to the foot contact point.

Trying leg lengths 0.64/0.6 instead, giving a shallower knee bend around 0.37m, which seems proportionate enough despite shortening the limb look. I'm also tapering the leg tube radius along its length and checking whether the two legs' inner edges overlap near the hip center, since the torso's hip width needs to properly bridge into the legs without gaps or clipping.

Now I'm defining the foot geometry as a block attached to the ankle bone, positioned to extend backward for a heel and forward into a toe region, then adding three toe chains branching from the ankle with tapered sweeps that narrow to a point for each digit.

Next I'm adding knee and shin detailing: a rock guard part at the knee joint, flattened and scaled for an armored look, plus I'm considering a glowing lava-textured torus ring wrapped around the shin as a decorative seam.

Then I'm sketching out thigh armor plates and extra rock details on the outer thigh, along with a crack decal placed on the front of the thigh to tie in the lava-cracked aesthetic.

For build order, I'm settling on defining skeleton joints (hips, spine, neck, head, jaw) first, then the arm and leg chains since they depend on the chest parent, leaving geometry placement flexible since it only needs the joints to exist. I'm also noting that since I always explicitly assign colors to every shape, the "nearest part" color inheritance rule won't be an issue here.

For the ground, I'm attaching a dark rock cylinder base to the hips bone using flat shading, then layering a smaller glowing lava-colored disc on top to form the lake, considering whether to make the lava lake edge irregular rather than a perfect circle.

Actually, I'll go with a thin lava disc with a glow effect, positioned so the feet sink slightly into the pool, giving the impression the golem stands molten pool-side. I'm scattering rim rocks around the pool's edge for texture and sketching radial crack sweeps across the rock ring to add surface detail.

For embellishment I'm placing floating rocks and small glowing lava crystal octahedra near the hips, then adding a cluster of three glowing cone-shaped crystals sprouting from the upper back/shoulders for a dramatic Genshin-style molten crystal effect.

Now I'm generating a row of flame card frames across the shoulders and back, then feeding those into a cards helper that creates billboard flame meshes with cross orientation, randomized variation, and spin, followed by applying a glow boost to the resulting flame meshes.

I'm scattering additional ember cards randomly around the body—small, upward-facing, glowing cards with varied sizes and positions—plus a few flame frames arcing over the head to form a crown effect, and setting up a local-position helper for placing head details relative to the head bone.

Now I'm blocking out the skull and brow geometry: a dark rock box for the skull, a brow ridge box, and angled brow wedges rotated to give an angry, menacing look above the eyes.

Now placing the eye geometry at the computed position with front-facing orientation, flipping UVs for the left eye, and checking that the brow depth protrudes slightly beyond the skull's front face.

I'm confirming the eye sits just below the brow with correct spacing, then blocking out the nose/snout, cheek plates, and starting the upper jaw geometry with appropriate rock materials.

Now I'm positioning the upper jaw to overlap the skull base, adding a row of cone-shaped teeth angled downward, and laying out the lower jaw box in a darker rock tone.

Still placing more head details...

Good, that short neck path works since the skull bottom sits around y≈2.93. Now I'm adding dorsal rocks and back crystals, then placing a glowing crack decal on the torso front, working out the z-position based on the torso's curved profile at that height.

I realize a more robust way to position decals is to cast a ray against the skin mesh to find the exact surface point, so I'm writing a helper function that fires a ray forward or backward at a given x/y and returns the hit point, falling back to an estimated depth if nothing's hit. I'm confirming the decal function accepts a Vector3 point for placement, then moving on to work out the torso's box-section geometry.

Now I'm sketching out details like a waist belt built from a sweep along a closed loop path, a gem buckle made from scaled octahedrons with gold and lava-colored inner gems, and rock plate accents for the shoulders. I'm also checking TypeScript typing concerns around the ray helper's optional chaining, and starting to think through how the texture atlas should work -- using white tint colors for parts that get image textures versus solid colors for untextured parts.

I'm confirming that `texture` is a valid option on both part and stick functions, and that glow effects work correctly whether a part uses a flat color, a texture map, or comes from sweep/spike/decal/cards helpers, since they all expose compatible mesh data. I'm also starting to tally up the flat color palette to make sure I stay within the 64-color limit, listing out the lava tones, gold variants, and horn colors I'll need.

Now I'm checking which imports I actually need to avoid unused-import TypeScript errors, deciding to keep THREE, createBuilder, frame, rng, catmull, bezier, polyline, limb, svg, mottle, patches, cel, and glow while dropping paint, aim, and cells since they won't be used. Writing circle texture generation...

I'm sizing the circle so it sits mostly hidden beneath the golem's feet, scaling the radius to match a 1.9m pool, with a glowing orange disc beneath the texture.

Writing eye SVG shape...

Adjusting skirt geometry...

Setting up imports and a vector helper, then starting on the horn geometry generation code...

I'm checking the overall height budget, roughly 3.9-4m for the golem, and considering trimming the horn slightly to keep proportions reasonable. Now I'm working out how head.local resolves into a Vector3 for positioning, then starting to build the jaw hierarchy.

Now I'm placing glowing crystal cones along the back near the chest bone, each tilted backward with a dark rock base beneath it, adjusting the vertical offset so the base sits flush against the cone's bottom.

Still placing the rocks, cones, and flame positions relative to the crystals, then assigning bone attachments for parts without an obvious joint—defaulting to hips where needed. Time to finalize all these coordinates and write the full layout.

Toes don't need special treatment. I'm verifying the skirt sweep callback signature uses the path point's position correctly, then moving to the pectoral extrusion, shaping each side with a polygon profile oriented along the chest surface normal with thickness and bevel.

I check the thickness axis direction cross-product and confirm it points outward correctly, leaving the outline sharp-cornered without smoothing. The torso patches and remaining paint placements are mostly settled, so I'm finalizing the plan before writing the complete build.
